events.description: A large, sudden explosion erupts on the port side of the ship, with a bright white fireball and black smoke plume rising rapidly.
A second major explosion occurs near the center of the ship, producing an even larger fireball and expanding smoke cloud; the first explosion's effects are still visible.
The explosion intensifies and propagates along the ship’s superstructure; multiple fireballs and dense smoke dominate the vessel, indicating ongoing detonations or fuel ignition.
Continued violent combustion with large flames and billowing smoke; the ship is engulfed, suggesting secondary explosions or structural failure from prior blasts.
Sustained explosive fire with reduced peak intensity but still significant flame and smoke output; the explosion phase transitions toward conflagration.

A large, violent explosion erupts from the midsection of the warship, producing a massive fireball and dense smoke plume; the blast appears to be a single detonation event initiating the destruction sequence.
A secondary, smaller explosion occurs near the bow of the ship, visible as a bright flash and localized fireball amid ongoing burning; distinct from the initial main blast.
A large, bright flash and expanding fireball erupts from the midsection of the burning ship, accompanied by a plume of smoke and debris—indicative of a secondary explosion.
A second distinct explosive burst occurs near the forward section of the ship, visible as a sudden bright orange-white flash and upward ejection of flame and smoke, separate from the ongoing fire.
A bright flash and initial fireball erupt at the stern of the ship, indicating a sudden explosive event; visible in frame f0 (12.5s) as the first clear sign of detonation.
Secondary explosion or rapid fire propagation occurs shortly after the initial blast, with intensified flames and smoke plume expanding; supported by frames f0–f1 showing escalation within ~0.5s.
